Subject: Audit logs: retention, exports, and deletion — quick questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing procurement & security sign-off and have a few concrete questions so the review loop can move quickly: 

- What is Redwood's default retention for audit/access logs in the hosted offering (events that show token usage, route, model, timestamp, requester id)?
- Do you support a one-click bulk export for a tenant's full audit history (e.g., last 12 months) or only incremental/event streams?
- In what formats can exports be delivered (NDJSON/JSON/CSV), and can exports be pushed to our S3 bucket in us-east-1?
- If we request deletion of logs for residency reasons, what is your deletion workflow and how do you provide proof of deletion? Are backups removed as well?
- Any SLA for exports (how long until we receive the delivered archive)?

I've attached our security questionnaire (Finvero-Security-Questionnaire.pdf) — the procurement team will want clear answers for the retention and deletion proofs section. 

Appreciate a concise summary and any links to docs/KB. We can schedule a 30-min call if helpful.

Best,
Miguel
Head of Security, Finvero

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Audit logs: retention, exports, and deletion — quick questions

Thanks Miguel — good questions. High-level answers below and then Neha will add export schema/details. I'm also looping in Sergio for legal/compliance language around deletion certification.

Summary (hosted Redwood API):
- Default retention (hosted): 90 days for access/audit logs (request metadata, route, model, timestamp, requester id).
- Export: We provide both streaming event APIs for near-real-time ingestion and a bulk export API that can produce NDJSON or CSV archives for specified time ranges. Bulk exports can be delivered to a customer-owned S3 bucket (us-east-1 supported).
- Export window: For hosted customers, ad-hoc bulk exports are available for up to 12 months of history. For Dedicated/Private deployments you can configure longer retention via contract.
- Formats & fields: NDJSON (preferred), gzipped CSV also available. Exports contain request id, device ip (anonymized if requested), model, tokens_in/out, timestamp, tenant_id, and action_type.
- Deletion: For hosted, deletion requests remove the primary index and stop retention; backups are on a rolling schedule (we retain short-term backups up to 30 days beyond primary retention for disaster recovery). For Private (customer-hosted) we support contractual certified deletion with KMS key-escrow workflows and a deletion manifest.
- Proof: We provide an export manifest (CSV) listing deleted file keys and checksums. For Dedicated/Private we can provide signed attestations as part of the DPA addendum.
- SLA: Typical bulk export turnaround is 48–72 hours for hosted. Dedicated customers get higher-priority processing (24 hours).

Attachments: audit_export_schema.pdf (schema summary) — see Neha's message for examples.

If OK, I'll open a ticket to schedule the export sample and patch the questionnaire responses into a short email for procurement. Want to hop on a call tomorrow morning?

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Audit logs: retention, exports, and deletion — export schema & process

Hi Miguel — adding some technical specifics so procurement has what they need:

1) Fields included (export):
- event_id
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- tenant_id
- user_id (obfuscated/requester_id)
- request_id
- api_route
- model_name
- prompt_tokens / completion_tokens
- outcome_status (200/4xx/5xx)
- response_latency_ms
- token_hash (SHA256) — note: we do not export raw prompt text unless explicitly requested in the export scope and contractually approved.

2) Example NDJSON line (single event):
{
  "event_id": "evt_01G8V8...",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-18T08:59:23Z",
  "tenant_id": "finvero-prod",
  "user_id": "usr_...",
  "request_id": "req_...",
  "api_route": "/v1/generate",
  "model_name": "redwood-3b",
  "prompt_tokens": 42,
  "completion_tokens": 128,
  "outcome_status": 200,
  "response_latency_ms": 180,
  "token_hash": "a3f4..."
}

3) Export mechanics:
- Method A: Console request -> background job -> bucket push (you provide AWS role/ARN).
- Method B: API request with time-range -> returns pre-signed archive URL.
- Incremental exports: We support delta exports using checkpoint cursors for frequent pulls.

4) Size & timing estimates:
- Roughly 1GB per million events (varies with fields & compression).
- Hosted bulk export for ~30 days of heavy usage (tens of millions of events) may take 24–72 hours to compile and deliver.

5) Deletion & backups:
- Hosted: primary deletion occurs as requested/at retention boundary. Short-term backups retained up to 30 days for recovery — these are purged on a 30-day schedule.
- Private/Dedicated: we can implement zero-backup deletion or customer-managed backups.
- Certified deletion: available for Private & Enterprise Dedicated customers with an attestation signed by our Compliance team.

6) How to request (recommended):
- Open a security export request via support.redwood.com with: tenant_id, time range, export format, delivery method (S3/API), and legal contact. Attach any NDAs/DPA references.

I've attached requested_export_manifest.csv as a sample manifest format we provide at delivery. Happy to produce a small sample export for your dev/security team to validate.

—Neha
Sr. Product Manager, Security & Privacy
